summary: Flaky: storefront call-budget tests fail under load, and one fails OPEN (TKT-216 gate incidental)
description:
**Flaky under load, found while gating TKT-216.**

`web/storefront/test/page-call-budget.test.ts` (TKT-208's call-budget proof) fails three of its six
cases when the machine is busy:

```
× event list renders on exactly one upstream call      (timeout at 5000ms)
× event detail renders on exactly one upstream call    (timeout at 5000ms)
× festival detail renders on exactly one upstream call (expected length 1, got 2)
```

**It is not a regression.** Verified by checking out the parent commit (`a05d5cc6`, a docs-only
change sitting on a gate that was green) and reproducing all three failures there. Verified further
by re-running with `--testTimeout=30000`: **6 passed, twice.** The transform step alone takes ~9.7s
in these runs, against a 5s per-test default.

**Why it matters beyond the noise.** The third failure is the interesting one: it does not time out,
it counts **two** upstream calls where the budget allows one. That is the assertion TKT-208 exists to
make, and if load can make it report two calls, then the test cannot distinguish "the page made a
second call" from "the machine was busy". A call-budget proof that fails open under load is not
proving the budget.

**Suggested direction (not a decision):**
- Raise the per-test timeout for this file so a slow transform cannot be read as a budget violation.
- Separately, work out whether the 2-call observation is a genuine second fetch triggered by a
  timeout/retry path, or an artefact of the stub counting a cancelled request. Those need different
  fixes, and only the second is harmless.

Do not simply raise the timeout and close it: that hides the second question.

---

**Update (TKT-216 gate, same session).** The per-test timeout in that file was raised to 30s, because
the gate must be green and the 5s default was turning machine load into a reported budget violation.
The three failures stop reproducing.

**That change closes the noise, not this ticket.** The substantive question is untouched and is the
reason this ticket stays open:

> one of the three observed failures did NOT time out — it counted **two** upstream calls where the
> budget allows one.

So the assertion can still fail **open**. What remains to determine is whether a second fetch is ever
genuine (a retry path, a cancelled request the stub double-counts) or purely an artefact. Those need
different fixes and only one of them is harmless. A comment in the test now says the same thing, so
whoever raises the timeout again does not read it as resolved.

governingAdrs.why: Rule 3 (frontends are call-frugal) is what this test proves; TKT-208 built it.

reference.summary: The failing file and the budget it asserts
Found while gating TKT-216; reproduced at the parent commit, so not caused by it

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Implementation readiness — CONCERNS (shaped 2026-08-08)

Filed with a good description and never shaped, so Gate 1 has been hard-blocking it. Shaped now.

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Objective | OK | The assertion must fail closed, not open |
| Scope | OK | The budget test and the fetch path behind it |
| Uncertainties | **WARN** | Genuine second fetch vs stub artefact — unanswered, and it IS the ticket |
| Dependencies | OK | None; the TKT-216 timeout bump already isolated the signal |
| Approach | **WARN** | Follows from the uncertainty; cannot be settled in shaping |
| AC verifiable | OK | Must demonstrate the test can still fail |
| Context-mémo | OK | Re-resolved today |

**Concern worth stating plainly:** two `open` items would normally block Gate 1, and they are left
open deliberately — this is an *investigation* ticket whose product is an answer, not a diff. If the
owner prefers, it should be re-typed as a **Spike** with the fix as a follow-up; that is a cleaner
fit for the pipeline than a Story carrying two open uncertainties.

**The reason to prioritize it anyway:** this is the only known assertion in the repo that can pass
while the property it proves is false. Per `AGENTS.md`, a fixture that cannot show the negative is a
recurring defect class here (TKT-61, and the "fixture too small" learning). This is that class,
caught in the act.

objective.note: The call-budget assertion cannot report a violation that machine load caused, and cannot pass while a genuine second fetch happens. It must fail CLOSED.

scope.note: web/storefront/test/page-call-budget.test.ts and whatever in the storefront fetch path explains a second call. Not a re-litigation of TKT-208's budget itself.

uncertainties.note: OPEN and this is the ticket: is the observed 2-call count a genuine second fetch (a retry or revalidation path) or an artefact of the stub counting a cancelled request? Different fixes, and only the artefact is harmless. Nobody has yet determined which.

dependencies.note: None. The 30s timeout raised during TKT-216's gate already removed the load-induced noise, so the remaining signal can be studied in isolation.

approach.note: OPEN, and depends on the answer above. If genuine: the budget or the page is wrong. If artefact: the stub's counting is wrong. Do NOT raise the timeout again and close - a comment in the test already warns against exactly that.

first_slice.note: Reproduce the 2-call observation deliberately (load the machine, or drive the stub directly) so the question can be answered from evidence rather than inference.

success.note: A test that fails when a second upstream call genuinely happens, and passes under load. Prove the failing direction works - a budget proof that cannot fail is the defect being fixed.

context_memo.note: Re-resolved 2026-08-08. The TKT-216 timeout change and its in-test warning comment are on main.
